metadata.title: [Bugfix][Core] Backport vllm-project/vllm#66048, #45224, #44490, #54436, #51694, #47911, #52142: resample race, shm reader stalls, new_block_ids leak, PP broadcast, MM block hashing, compile cache
metadata.body:
## Purpose

Seven upstream bug fixes for the speculative decoding, scheduler, pipeline-parallel, prefix-cache and compile-cache paths, one commit each. None of them is on main; each commit message has the details.

vllm-project/vllm#66048 ([BugFix] Fix/spec decode insert resampled race, upstream commit 4d82b5691, by shustovTE). _insert_resampled_kernel in vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py loads num_sampled, stores num_sampled + 1 to the same address and then keeps using the loaded value. With the default four warps nothing orders the warps of a program, so a later warp can read the incremented counter. In the PTX that Triton 3.6 emits for sm_70 and sm_75, both stores (counter and token) are issued by thread 0 alone, with the value it loaded before its own store, so such a warp cannot put a token, bonus or resampled, in the wrong slot or increment the counter twice. It does load expanded_idx_mapping one entry further and then the temperature at the index found there. For the last request of a batch whose drafts were all accepted, that entry is past the end of the mapping (allocated with one entry per logit), and the temperature load can fault; upstream found this out-of-range access in two CUDA core dumps. These loads come before the greedy early return, so greedy requests are exposed as well. On main rejection_sample, and with it this kernel, runs in every verification step of the Model Runner V2 RejectionSampler (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py) that does not take a dedicated sparse path, and in the DFlash2 sampler paths. Applied unchanged: the launch gets num_warps=1, like the neighbouring _rejection_kernel.

vllm-project/vllm#45224 ([Bugfix][Core] shm_broadcast: bound idle reader waits and release read slots, upstream commit 10c75477b, by chaeminlim-mb). Two faults in the MessageQueue reader (vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py). An idle reader with indefinite=True got timeout_ms() == None and parked on the ZMQ notify socket without a bound; the notify PUB socket drops silently (SNDHWM=1), so one lost notify left the reader asleep although the data was in the ring. And the read flag was set after the yield, so an exception in the caller's with-block left the slot unread and the writer blocked on it. The workers of the multiproc executor read the RPC queue with indefinite=True (vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py), so a lost notify stalls a worker until VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (300 s) ends the engine core. Source and tests are upstream's unchanged; only the context of the new constant differs, because main already has #1306 (busy readers poll the notify socket, SHM_NOTIFY_POLL_INTERVAL_S), which fixes a different fault. The fix does not depend on the vllm-project/vllm#60472 backport in #1406 (upstream merged #45224 first); both add tests before test_warning_logs, so whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase of tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py (keep both test blocks).

vllm-project/vllm#44490 ([Bugfix][Core] Fix host memory leak from undrained new_block_ids, upstream commit b4cfbc24d, by Sunt-ing). The KV cache managers (vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py) record every newly allocated attention block in new_block_ids, but the scheduler (vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py) drained the list only when KV cache zeroing is on, which needs_kv_cache_zeroing (vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py) ties to Mamba layers. For every model without Mamba layers, DeepSeek-V4 for example, the list grows by every allocated block for the lifetime of the engine. Adapted: only the scheduler hunk, which drains the list every step and uses it only for zeroing. Upstream also adds a switch in the managers that records only when zeroing is on; its hunk does not apply to main, and it would not cover CircularBufferManager._claim_ring_block and KpoolTailManager._allocate_tail_block, which record without a spec check, while draining on the consumer side covers every manager. Upstream has no test; test_new_block_ids_drained_without_kv_cache_zeroing is added to tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py.

vllm-project/vllm#54436 ([Bugfix][PP] Never drop a decoding request from the sampled-token broadcast, upstream commit 6bafc049a, by ArcheyChen). compute_need_sampled_mask (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py) dropped a row from the PP sampled-token broadcast once max(num_computed, prefill_len) + 1 reached prompt_len + max_tokens. With async scheduling and speculative decoding num_computed_tokens already counts the drafts of the step in flight, while the scheduler keeps scheduling the request; such a row misses the broadcast, the earlier stages keep stale last_sampled_tokens and draft_tokens, and the last up to k tokens and their KV go wrong. It is reachable under PP with async scheduling, speculative decoding, more than one running request and a request that sets max_tokens. We have not hit it: our PP5 setups run with max_num_seqs 1, where the engine core applies a step's output before the next schedule. Adapted: the upstream diff does not apply (main's PP handler, no pcp_manager.py), so the change is made by hand in upstream's form: the mask is produces_sample alone, and InputBatch.max_seq_len_np, which only the dropped check read, is removed from input_batch.py and model_runner.py. RequestState.max_seq_len and the max_tokens argument of RequestState.add_request stay, as upstream; upstream reads the field again from vllm-project/vllm#58542 on. Upstream's tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py is added unchanged; test_compute_need_sampled_mask in tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_pp.py is removed, two of its cases are covered by the new file and the third asserted the dropped behaviour.

vllm-project/vllm#51694 ([Bugfix][KV Cache] Fix incremental multimodal block hashing, upstream commit e6c07ea57, by CZT0). When a block is completed only by generated tokens, request_block_hasher (vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py) started the multimodal search at the last mm input, so an earlier image in the same block was missing from the hash keys: the block hashed differently than when computed fresh, and two requests with the same tokens but a different earlier image in that block could share it. It needs a hash block that holds several mm inputs and ends after the prompt, which hybrid models make easy: their hash block follows the attention block, which vLLM raises to the Mamba page size (it logs "Setting attention block size to 800 tokens" for Qwen3.8-27B FP8 on our V100s), so two small images with a short question fit into one block. This is a different path from #1363, which keys the partial prefix entries on image identity. Adapted: upstream finds the start index with a bisect helper, get_mm_features_in_window, which main does not have; here the search simply starts at the first mm input. _gen_mm_extra_hash_keys skips passed inputs and returns early for blocks after the last one, so decode blocks stay cheap. As upstream, _gen_mm_extra_hash_keys keeps its -1 ("last mm input") convention. Upstream's test is added unchanged.

vllm-project/vllm#47911 (fix: hash speculative draft model config, upstream commit 7cc2e8e74, by alexeldeib). SpeculativeConfig.compute_hash (vllm/config/speculative.py) took from an aux-hidden-state drafter (EAGLE3, extract_hidden_states, DFlash, DFlash2, DSpark) only that it uses aux hidden states and its layer ids, not the drafter's ModelConfig. The drafter compiles into the target's torch.compile cache directory, whose name comes from this hash, so swapping the drafter checkpoint (other weights or another quantization) under the same VLLM_CACHE_ROOT loads the old drafter's compiled graphs. The hash now includes draft_model_config.compute_hash(), so the first boot of a DFlash, DFlash2, DSpark or EAGLE3 setup after this change compiles anew; MTP is unchanged. Adapted: the hunk is placed by hand because main's mtp_expert_quantization factor sits between the upstream context lines, and the generated docs/design/architecture/runtime_reference.md is refreshed (the two new lines move SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__; without it check-architecture-reference fails). Upstream has no test; test_draft_model_config_is_hashed is added to tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark.py.

vllm-project/vllm#52142 ([Bugfix] Fix standalone torch.compile cache loading after relocation, upstream commit cb4f016c5, by jungjiyu). InductorStandaloneAdaptor.load (vllm/compilation/compiler_interface.py) opened the artifact at handle[1], the absolute path written into vllm_compile_cache.py when the graph was saved, while saving builds the path from the current cache directory and the key. A cache root that was copied or moved therefore reads its artifacts from the old root while that exists and fails to load once it is gone. Our cache roots are copies of older ones, and their handles point into the roots they were copied from; in one of them a hash directory points into a root that is already deleted, so a boot that hits that hash would fail. Applied unchanged: load joins self.cache_dir with handle[0]; upstream's tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py is added.

Not a duplicate: I searched the open and closed PRs and issues of this repository for each upstream number (66048, 45224, 44490, 54436, 51694, 47911, 52142), the PRs also for insert_resampled, resampled, num_warps, shm_broadcast, MessageQueue, acquire_read, notify socket, new_block_ids, take_new_block_ids, kv cache zeroing, need_sampled_mask, compute_need_sampled_mask, sampled-token broadcast, max_seq_len_np, block hash multimodal, extra hash keys, draft_model_config, draft model config hash, standalone compile, vllm_compile_cache and compile cache, and the issues for insert_resampled, shm_broadcast, new_block_ids, need_sampled, multimodal block hash, draft model hash and compile cache; none backports or fixes these faults. Related: #1306 (merged) and #1406 (open, vllm-project/vllm#60472) change shm_broadcast.py for other faults, see above; #1363 (merged) covers partial prefix entries, not full-block hashes; #1276 (open, lookahead block hashes) touches kv_cache_utils.py, scheduler.py and speculative.py as well, the sources merge without conflict and only the generated runtime_reference.md would need a refresh.

AI assistance was used for these backports. I reviewed every line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

CPU, on this branch without native libraries:
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_pp.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark.py tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py
For every new test, the same test with the corresponding source file reset to main.
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD; pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD

GPU:
python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py
python -m pytest tests/kernels/core/test_dflash2_sampler_graph.py tests/kernels/core/test_sm70_sampler_graph_branch.py
python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_pp.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _insert_resampled_kernel (spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py) | any logits dtype | every rejection_sample call on Model Runner V2, one program per request | same kernel, launched with one warp | source; upstream core-dump analysis; executed: tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py on V100 and RTX 8000 | the race itself needs warp timing; no deterministic reproducer |
| MessageQueue reader (shm_broadcast.py) | n/a | idle reader with indefinite=True; caller raising inside acquire_read | idle reader rechecks the written flag every 5 s; read flag set in finally | executed: tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py | Ray and multi-node remote readers not run |
| Scheduler new_block_ids drain (sched/scheduler.py) | n/a | KV cache config without Mamba groups | list drained every step; used only when zeroing is on | executed: tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py | host memory of a long-running engine not measured |
| PP sampled-token broadcast (worker/gpu/pp_utils.py) | n/a | PP >= 2, async scheduling, speculative decoding, request at its max_tokens cap | every row that produces a sample is broadcast | executed: tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py; fork A/B on PP5 | PP with several running requests not run on this branch |
| request_block_hasher (core/kv_cache_utils.py) | n/a | block completed by generated tokens holding more than one mm input | same block hash as a fresh computation | executed: tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py, tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py | multimodal end-to-end request not run |
| SpeculativeConfig.compute_hash (config/speculative.py) | n/a | EAGLE3, extract_hidden_states, DFlash, DFlash2, DSpark with a draft model config | drafter ModelConfig hash is a factor; MTP unchanged | executed: tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark.py | first boot of these setups recompiles |
| InductorStandaloneAdaptor.load (compilation/compiler_interface.py) | binary and unpacked artifacts | cache root copied or moved | artifact loaded from cache_dir/key | executed: tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py | none |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: always on; bug fixes, not a performance change.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: none.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: n/a (no benchmark on this branch; not a performance change).
- Wheel SHA or source commit: this branch on main c98a8d664; the same fixes run on our fork (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, 0b342e7b5; there the vllm-project/vllm#54436 backport also drops the then unread RequestState.max_seq_len, and the vllm-project/vllm#51694 backport the then unused -1 convention of _gen_mm_extra_hash_keys).
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used: none for the tests.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: not a performance change. A/B on our fork with these fixes (DeepSeek-V4 and GLM-5.3, PP5): speed and texts unchanged.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: not touched.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: no setting added or changed.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: none; docs/design/architecture/runtime_reference.md regenerated for moved line numbers only.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: none.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no change.

## Test Result

On this branch (main c98a8d664 + these seven commits), CPU, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="":
- tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py: 13 passed. Without the shm_broadcast.py change the four new cases fail (missing SHM_READER_RECHECK_INTERVAL_MS; read flag 0 after the raising reader).
- tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py: 109 passed, 1 failed; tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py: 13 passed, 1 failed. Both failures are the same on main c98a8d664: test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders needs two GPUs, test_abort_request_when_structured_output_fsm_cannot_advance fails with "'AsyncScheduler' object has no attribute 'mixed_prefill_budget'". The new test fails without the scheduler change.
- tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py: 4 passed; tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_pp.py: 7 passed, 1 failed (test_runner_accepts_pp2_with_ple_layers_on_first_rank: "No CUDA GPUs are available", same on main). For upstream's capped decoding row (num_computed 14176, prefill_len 12175, 8 scheduled, cap 14175) the old mask returns None, the new one [True].
- tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py: 73 passed; tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py: 91 passed. The new test fails without the kv_cache_utils.py change (2 failed).
- tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark.py: 16 passed. The new test fails without the speculative.py change.
- tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py: 2 passed; both fail without the compiler_interface.py change.
- tests/v1/streaming_input/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_streaming.py, which also builds a RequestState, errors on main and on this branch alike ("RequestState.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'model_dtype'").
- pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: every hook passes except check-layering, which reports vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py (platform coupling 25 -> 32) and vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py (37 -> 39); this PR touches neither file, the report is the same on main c98a8d664.
- pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: passed.

GPU, on main c98a8d664 built here with this branch's Python files (native libraries unchanged by this PR), one pytest process per file, once on a Tesla V100 (SM70) and once on a Quadro RTX 8000 (SM75):
- tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py: 81 passed on both.
- tests/v1/spec_decode/test_synthetic_rejection_sampler_utils.py: 9 passed on both.
- tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_pp.py: 8 passed on both.
- tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders on two V100s: 1 passed (also on main).
- tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py: 13 passed on both (run one card at a time; started on both cards at once, the multi-process tests of this file collide on the host).
- tests/kernels/core/test_dflash2_sampler_graph.py and tests/kernels/core/test_sm70_sampler_graph_branch.py: on the V100 4 failed and 2 failed with this branch, and exactly the same on plain main c98a8d664 (TypeError: the test fakes lack the `allow_penalties`, `block` and `has_floor` arguments the current kernels take); skipped on the RTX 8000. Not related to this PR.

Applied unchanged: load joins self.cache_dir with handle[0]; upstream's tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py is added.

Not a duplicate: I searched the open and closed PRs and issues of this repository for each upstream number (66048, 45224, 44490, 54436, 51694, 47911, 52142), the PRs also for insert_resampled, resampled, num_warps, shm_broadcast, MessageQueue, acquire_read, notify socket, new_block_ids, take_new_block_ids, kv cache zeroing, need_sampled_mask, compute_need_sampled_mask, sampled-token broadcast, max_seq_len_np, block hash multimodal, extra hash keys, draft_model_config, draft model config hash, standalone compile, vllm_compile_cache and compile cache, and the issues for insert_resampled, shm_broadcast, new_block_ids, need_sampled, multimodal block hash, draft model hash and compile cache; none backports or fixes these faults. Related: #1306 (merged) and #1406 (open, vllm-project/vllm#60472) change shm_broadcast.py for other faults, see above; #1363 (merged) covers partial prefix entries, not full-block hashes; #1276 (open, lookahead block hashes) touches kv_cache_utils.py, scheduler.py and speculative.py as well, the sources merge without conflict and only the generated runtime_reference.md would need a refresh.
